observation.description: v1's private-roster posture forecloses a host/moderator removing another member: id-addressed ctx.membership.remove requires a private row id the app can never obtain, and the transition grammar's other-targeted operations are unreachable for removal. For group chat this rules out kick/ban — a table-stakes moderation operation — so A2-10 (revocation stops delivery to an already-connected client) was proven through self-revocation (leaveChannel), which exercised the same barrier: the established protected live handle blanked in ~1.7s, a post-revocation commit was not delivered, and the fresh read denial was the uniform SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED {kind:'role'}.

competitorOutcome.description: The frozen Convex chat arm implemented host-driven membership revocation directly (membership documents are app data): Bob's established private watch errored, fresh reads were denied, and a subsequent private message was not delivered.

mustNotRegress: The revocation-active live barrier (blank-then-terminal-deny on an established handle) and the non-disclosing uniform denial, both proven by this arm.
smallestCoherentFix: A declared other-targeted remove/setRole transition reachable without a private row id — e.g. principal-addressed generated commands (ctx.membership.<decl>.removePrincipal(resource, principal)) admitted only when the declaration's transition matrix authorizes the caller class, keeping the roster unenumerable.
acceptanceWitness: Host removes a member by principal; the removed member's established live handle blanks and post-revocation commits are not delivered (the A2-10 shape, other-initiated); an unauthorized caller's attempt is the uniform role denial.
